sentences.text:
This is a claim petition U/Sec.166 of MV Act claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- with interest for the injuries suffered by the petitioner in the Motor Vehicle Accident occurred on 09.02.2023.
2.

The averments of the petition in brief is as follows:
On 09.02.2023 at about 7.30 p.m. the petitioner was proceeding by riding the Bike bearing No. KA.02.ES.8160 near Rudresh house, Halenijagal village, at that time the driver of the Car bearing No. KA.52.M.6213 driven the same at high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against petitioner from behind and caused the accident.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to District Government Hospital, Tumkur,
wherein first aid treatment was given and shifted to Victoria hospital, Bengaluru,
wherein petitioner took treatment as an inpatient and also underwent surgery.
The petitioner has spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical and conveyance charges etc.,
Prior to the accident, petitioner was aged about 35 years, doing coolie work and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
Due to accidental injuries, petitioner has lost his earning capacity.
The 1st respondent being the insurer and the 2 nd respondent being the owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence, this petition.
3. In spite of service of notice, 2nd respondent - owner has not appeared before the court, hence placed as Exparte.
After service of summons, 1st respondent - Insurance company appeared through it's counsel and filed written statement.

4. The written statement averments of the 1 st respondent are hereunder:
This respondent has filed written statement by contending that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant and without any basis.

Further it has admitted the issuance of insurance policy with respect to Car bearing No.
KA.52.M.6213 vide policy No. 3311/00730317/000/00 which was in force as on the date of accident, however, the liability of this respondent if any is subject to terms and conditions of policy.

sentences.text: Inter-alia contended that the driver of the Car was not holding a valid and effective driving license as on the date of the alleged accident.
Further contended that, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(b) of MV Act.
Further it has denied the cause and manner of accident, age, avocation and income of the petitioner, injuries sustained and also the amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings, this tribunal has framed the following :ISSUES:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 09.02.2023 at about 7.30 p.m. when he was proceeding as a rider on the Bike bearing No. KA.02.ES.8160, near Rudresh's house,
Halenijagal village, Sompura hobli, Nelamangala taluk, he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident due to rash or negligent driving of the Car bearing No.
KA.52.M.6213 by its driver as stated in the petition?
2. Whether the petitioner proves that he is entitled for the compensation?

If so, to what extent and from whom?
3. What order or award?
6. In order to prove the case, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and marked Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.15.
Further, Dr. B Ramesh, Orthopaedic surgeon at Victoria hospital is examined as PW.2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P16 to Ex.P19.
P.W.1 & P.W.2 were cross-
examined from the side of respondent No.1.
In spite of sufficient opportunity respondent No.1 has not lead any evidence.
7. Heard the arguments from both side.
8. Perused the records placed before the Tribunal.

The findings of this Tribunal to the above referred Issues are as under:-
Issue No.1 :- In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 :- In the partly Affirmative.

Issue No.3 :- As per the final order, for the following:
:REASONS:
9. ISSUE No.1:-

Before going to discuss the issue no.1, it is worth to refer the decision reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 between Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that, "it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied".

Therefore it is crystal clear that the petitioner has to prove his case on the Naveen Kumar H.R vs Cholamandalam Ms Gen Ins Co Ltd on 7 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96571885/
3 principle of preponderance of probabilities.

sentences.text: 10. In order to prove this issue, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 by way of filing affidavit in support of his oral examination-in-chief.
Hence, this Tribunal need not to recapitulate the same once again at this juncture.
P.W.1 has relied on Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.10.
Accordingly, Ex.P.1 is the true copy of complaint.
Ex. P.2
is the true copy of FIR.
Ex . P3
is the true copy of spot panchanama.
Ex . P4
is the true copy of charge sheet.
Ex . P5
is the true copy of IMV report.
Ex. P6
& P7 are the notice and reply to the notice U/Sec.133.
Ex.P8 is the true copy of wound certificate.
Ex. P.9
& P10 are the discharge summaries.
11. According to the petitioner, he has sustained injuries in the road accident.
According to the 1 st respondent- Insurance company, the offending vehicle was not at all involved in the accident and the motor vehicle was falsely implicated in the accident.
The petitioner has filed the petition after thought by twisting the facts to get compensation.
12. In the instant case, the petitioner has produced police documents.
As per Ex.P.1, complaint was lodged before Dobbespet Police Station on 10.02.2023.
Thereafter, as per Ex.P.1, FIR was lodged against the driver of Car bearing No. KA.52.M.6213.

Further, on careful perusal of Ex.P.1, Ex.P.2 and Ex.P.4 it appears to this Tribunal that, on the basis of complaint, the police have registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle and Investigating officer has submitted Charge sheet as per Ex.P.4 after completing investigation.

A careful perusal of Ex.P.8, it clearly goes to show that,
the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

Further, on perusal of Ex.P.4 i.e.,
final report, it reveals that, the driver of offending vehicle i.e., Car bearing No. KA.52.M.6213 is arrayed as accused.

13. At the cost of repetition, the contents of complaint and charge sheet clearly reveals that, when the petitioner was proceeding by riding the motor cycle bearing No. KA.02.ES.8160 near Rudresh house, Halenijagal village, at that time the driver of Car bearing No. KA.52.M.6213 came in a rash or negligent manner with high and dashed to the petitioner from behind.
The evidence placed on record clearly reveals that the driver of Car bearing No. KA.52.M.6213 has caused the accident.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
14. ISSUE No.2:- This issue is with respect to entitlement of relief.
Already this Tribunal has observed that, accident was occurred due to rash or negligent driving of the driver of Car bearing No. KA.52.M.6213.
The 1st respondent is the insurer and the 2nd respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
Before going to discuss other aspects, it is appropriate to discuss the age and income of the petitioner.
15. Age:- According to the petitioner, he was aged about 35 years as on the date of accident.
In order to substantiate the same, the petitioner has produced Ex.P.13, the notarized copy of his Aadhaar Card.
On perusal of this document it appears to this Tribunal that, the date of birth of petitioner is mentioned as 10.12.1988.
The accident was occurred on 09.02.2023.
Hence, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident is 35 years.
Accordingly the age of the petitioner is considered as 35 years.

4 16. Income:-

entities.text: Naveen Kumar H.R vs Cholamandalam Ms Gen Ins Co Ltd on 7 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant case, the petitioner has stated that, he was doing Coolie work and earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
Per-contra, the 1st respondent has denied the income of petitioner.
To substantiate the income of petitioner, he has not placed any documentary evidence.

At this juncture, it is worth to rely on the decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka decided in M.F.A. No.101144 of 2020 ( MV-I) on 05.07.2023, between Ananda Vs. Arun and Another, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Para 9 (b) as hereunder:
" In the absence of any cogent material on record, it is for the courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant".
17.

In the absence of authentic document and supportive evidence, the notional income of the petitioner is to be considered by relying on the judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka referred to above.
As per the notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident in the year 2023 is Rs.16,000/- per month.
It is pertinent to note that, the accident took place on 09.02.2023.

Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,000/-
per month by adopting the chart given by the KSLSA.
18. Loss of Future Income due to disability:-
In the instant case, the petitioner has averred that, he has sustained grievous injuries to his right leg.
He has produced wound certificate, which is marked as Ex.P8.
On perusal of Ex.P.8 -Wound certificate
it reveals that, the petitioner has sustained laceration over right knee joint.

It is relevant to mention that, respondent No.1 has disputed the injuries caused to P.W.1.
19.
In order to prove the physical disability/injuries, the petitioner examined medical witness namely Dr. B Ramesh, Orthopaedic Surgeon, Victoria hospital, Bangalore as P.W.2.
This witness has filed the affidavit in lieu of evidence and stated that the petitioner has sustained Right open type 3B proximal tibia fracture with complete patella tender tear.

Further deposed that, he examined the petitioner on 27.02.2025 for the disability assessment and found that, the petitioner complains of pain in right knee, difficulty to squat on floor, sit cross legged, climb upstairs, walk in slope, kneel and stand on affected limb.
Finally he has assessed the permanent physical disability of right lower limbs at 30% and 15% to the whole body.
He was cross-examined from the side of respondent No.1 at length.
During the course of cross-examination, he has admitted that, he was not a treated doctor.
He has admitted that, fracture has been occurred below the patella bone.
Further he has admitted that, there is a fracture only in tibia bone.
He also admitted that implants are removed and fracture is united.
He also admitted that he has assessed only physical disability not functional disability and denied the suggestion regarding falsely assessed the disability to the whole body as 15%.
P.W.2 has produced 4 documents, where are marked as Ex.P.16 to Ex.P.19.

sentences.text: On perusal of the discharge summary of petitioner and evidence of medical witness clearly reveals that, petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and suffered physical disability.
However the doctor has clearly deposed that, he assessed only physical disability and not functional disability.
As per the evidence of PW.2 the fracture has been united and also implants have been removed.
Therefore, by considering the avocation of petitioner, the physical disability assessed by the P.W.2 is on higher side.
Hence, this Tribunal considered the functional disability of the injured as 5% to the whole body.
21. As discussed supra, age of the injured is considered as 35 years and his income is considered as Rs.16,000/- per month.
Annual income comes to Rs.1,92,000/-(16,000/- x 12).
Hence, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of injured as per Sarala Verma case is 16.
If we multiplied the yearly income with proper multiplier, then it comes to Rs.30,72,000/- (Rs.1,92,000/- X 16).
Already this Tribunal has considered the disability of petitioner as 5% to the whole body.
The same amount of Rs.1,53,600/- is awarded to the Injured/Petitioner under the head of loss of Future Income due to disabiltiy.
22. Medical Expenses:-
In the instant case, the petitioner has stated that, he has incurred Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance and nourishment chages etc.
In order to substantiate the incurring of medical expenses, the petitioner has produced medical bills marked at Ex.P14 amounting to Rs.4,139/- and prescriptions marked at Ex.P15.
This Tribunal has carefully perused Ex.P.14, the medical bills.
There is no contrary evidence from the respondents to disbelive the medical bills.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.4,139/- towards medical expenses.
23. Pain and suffering:-
According to the petitioner, immediately after the accident he was shifted to Victoria Hospital, wherein he was treated as an inpatient from 10.02.2023 to 28.02.2023 for a period of 19 days.
The doctors have advised him for regular follow-up treatment.
Already this Tribunal has observed that, the petitioner has taken certain treatment.
On perusal of Ex.P.8- Wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained fracture injuries.
On perusal of these documents it reveals that, the petitioner has sustained fracture injuries and taken treatment.
Further as per the evidence of doctor, it appears to this tribunal that, the petitioner has sustained physical disability.
There is no serious dispute with regard to inpatient for at about 19 days.

As such,
the petitioner suffered a lot of pain and inconvenience.
Considering all these aspects, the Tribunal grants compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings.

24. Loss of income during the laidup period:-
According to petitioner as per the advise of the doctors, he has taken follow-up treatment.
Already this Tribunal has observed that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and fractures.
Naturally it shows that, he might have taken at least two months rest because of the injuries.
The petitioner has averred that, he was doing Coolie work and earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
But he has not produced documents to substantiate the same.
Hence, this Tribunal has already assessed the income of petitioner as Rs.16,000/- per month.

As per Ex.P.9 & 10 discharge Naveen Kumar H.R vs Cholamandalam Ms Gen Ins Co Ltd on 7 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96571885/
6 summaries, the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient at Victoria hospital totally for the period of 19 days.

sentences.text: Hence, two months is to be considered as loss of income during laid-up period.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.32,000/- as compensation under the head of loss of income during laid up period.
25. Food, Nourishment and Atttendant charges:-
In so for as food, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges are concerned, the petitioner has taken conservative line of treatment.
The petitioner has not produced any documents in this regard.

Hence, looking to the injuries sustained and the period of treatment taken by the petitioner, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head of Food, Nourishment and Atttendant charges.
26. Loss of future amenities and happiness:- The petitioner was aged about 35 years at the time of accident.
The disability and physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Therefore, he might have suffered pain, discomforts in life and loss of amenities.
By considering the age, nature of injuries, percentage of disabiltiy, Rs.20,000/- is awarded under this head.

27. Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
 Heads Amount  1.Towards loss of Future income.

Rs. 1,53,600 /-
 2. Towards Medical Expenses.

Rs. 4,139 /-
 3. Towards Pain & Suffering.

Rs. 30,000/-
 4. Loss of income during the laidup  Rs. 32,000/-
 period

5. Food, Nourishment and Rs. 40,000/-
 Atttendant charges:
 6. Loss of future amenities and Rs. 20,000/-
 happiness.
Total.

Hence, petitioner is entitled for just and reasonable amount of Rs. 2,79,739/-
28.
Regarding liability and interest.
Driving License:-
According to the 1st respondent the driver of offending vehicle had not driving license.
However charge sheet submitted by IO does not reveals that the driver of offending vehicle was driving the vehicle without valid and effective DL.

Therefore, it appears to this Tribunal that,
the driver of the offending vehicle was holding valid D.L. to drive the offending vehicle at the time of Naveen Kumar H.R vs Cholamandalam Ms Gen Ins Co Ltd on 7 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96571885/

29. In view of the decision reported in MFA NO:
30131-2019 dtd, 12.5.2020 and M.F.A.No.100090/2014 C/w M.F.A.No.25107/2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and Others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and Another,

30. ISSUE No.3:-
In view of discussions made above, I proceed to pass the following.

:ORDER:
Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with costs of the petition.
Petitioner is awarded just and reasonable compensation of Rs. 2,79,739/- (Rupees Two lakhs seventy nine thousand seven hundred and thirty nine only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition to till the date of depositing of the compensation amount in the Tribunal.
Respondent No.1 shall deposit the compensation in the Tribunal within 2 months from the date of this judgment.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw Award Accordingly.
